Sfz Format sample player
The sfizz~ object uses the open-source Sfizz library to parse and play Sfz format files. These files define how samples are played and controlled from MIDI events. For more information and tutorials on the Sfz format, visit sfzformat.com. For information on the supported opcodes in the Sfizz library, visit sfz.tools.

Outputs
You can create an sfizz~ with more than two audio output channels with the outputs attribute. When using regular sfizz~ this attribute cannot be changed after the object is created so you need to supply it as a typed-in argument. To send audio from a sample to channels beyond 1 and 2, use the output opcode. output 0 means channels 1 + 2, output 1 means channels 3 + 4 and so on. So to use outputs 0 - 3 as in this example you need to create 8 output channels. Use the position opcode to pan a sound within the stereo field of each output pair.

The mc.sfizz~ object contains multiple sampler instances in one object using the MC wrapper. Each can read in its own Sfz file, or you can use the same file and control notes independently with MPE using the mc.miditarget object..
double-click to view and edit the dictionary

defaultpath modes:
0 - look for files in the search path (the default mode)
1 - use the value of the defaultpathname attribute
2 - use the location of the most recently opened Sfz file for this object (which won't work if you've never opened a file)
3 - use the location of the patcher (which don't work if the patcher hasn't been saved yet)
4- use the path specified by the default_path opcode in the control section of the dictionary
5 - use the Documents/Max 8/Library folder; subfolders of Library can be in the sample name
when needed, you should configure the default path location before sending the dictionary

Dictionaries - Sfz Format sample player
Instead of creating an Sfz file, you can define the behavior of the sfizz~ sampler using a Max dictionary. Entries in the dictionary correspond to Sfz opcodes. By default, sfizz~ looks for any sample files in the dictionary in the Max search path, but using the defaultpathmode and defaultpathname attributes, you can customize the location if you are referencing sample files that reside outside the search path.

MIDI - Sfz Format sample player
sfizz~ accepts midievent messages (produced by the midiparse and midiformat objects) but ignores channel information. By default sfizz~ is polyphonic up to 64 voices; this can be changed with the voices attribute. Details of voice allocation and repeated note handling can be set via opcodes in the Sfz file. You can also assign MIDI controllers to act on specific notes or globally in the Sfz file as demonstrated below.
